To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
kainate and AMPA receptors are involved in the induction of zifi268 and preprodymorphin mRNA in the striatum by a single injection, but not by repeated injections, of amphetamine.
the AMPH-induced increases in PPD and Zif/268 mRNAs in the rat striatum are blocked by DNQx pretreatment.

the induction of zifi268 and PPD gene expression in striatum by a single injection with AMPH was blocked by pretreatment with the kainate/AMP A receptor antagonist DNQX, while DNQX pretreat ment did not block the behavioral responses to AMPH, and that the constitutive expression of zif/ 268 gene in cortical, but not striatal, neurons was blocked by DN QX.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of kainates/AMPA receptors, and the immediate early gene, zif/268 in the behavioral and molecular responses to acute and chronic amphetamine.
the mechanisms underlying drug-induced changes in the brain.
the role of excitatory amino acids in the pathophysiology of drug abuse and in the development of sensitization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
kainate receptors play a role in the induction of striatal genes by amphetamine.
the kainate/AMP receptor system is involved in AMPH-induced sensitization of the dopamine system.
AMPH-induced changes in gene expression are mediated by different receptor systems, and these receptors may be differentially involved in the behavioral and molecular responses to AMPH.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

AMPH-induced behavioral responses are mediated by a variety of neurotransmitter receptors (e.g. dopamine and glutamate receptors) and that AMPH-induced increases in striatal zif-268 and PPD gene expression are mediated by glutamatergic kainate/AMP receptors.
the AMPH-induced increase in zif/268 in the caudata is mediated by a kainate receptor mechanism and the AMPH-induced decrease in zif/ 268 in the cortex is mediated by an AMPA receptor mechanism.
kainate receptors may play a role in the long-term behavioral and neurochemical effects of amphetamine, but not in the immediate effects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
kainate receptors may be a key component of AMPH sensitization.
the kainate/ AMPA receptor antagonist DNQX blocked the AMPH-induced increase in PPD mRNA in striatal neurons, but had no effect on the AMPH-induced locomotor activity.
kainate receptors play a role in the induction of zI/268 and prepro-dynorphin (ppd) mRNA by a single dose of amphetamine.
